title: George's ghost stories
summary: George told ghost stories after 10 pm, including a story of a gambler's dead mother sighing on a bridge.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Alan Jaffey somewhere around has a tape, which he's never been able to find. I guess he would find it sometime. George telling ghost stories. Did he ever tell ghost stories much?

Well, occasionally, but most of the time if he was going to tell, you know, it'd be after 10 o'clock. And some of my friends would be over and we'd start talking. Well, some would have to go on the corner around the corner. And they didn't want to hear it because they were afraid to go home. But he enjoyed telling tales and stories. But I never was one to sit down and really pay attention because I was kind of afraid myself. You were kind of what? Afraid.
Afraid. Afraid. Well, do you think he believed in this?
Well, that's kind of hard to answer. I would just say he actually believed in it, but some of the things he said that has happened will more or less make you stop and wonder.
Can you remember any of the things? Can you tell me some of the things he said?

Well, one particular story I remember very well was a man, he liked to gamble a lot. And his mother was Creole and she used to always scold him when he'd stay out late for gambling. And she used to sigh a lot, take a deep breath. So he just kept on gambling and eventually his mother got sick and she died. So he said it was one night late, about two or three in the morning, a man was coming home. And he had to cross over a little bridge like, and he saw this lady leaning over the bridge. So the man walked up to her and told her, don't jump. You know, things couldn't be that bad. So he said, the lady still was leaning on the rail and she didn't look up. She just took a deep sigh. And it scared him because that's what his mother used to always do. And he believed that that was his mother.
